title: Tiered KV demotion and lease coordination to guarantee correctness under continuous batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and long-running KV cache entries create a correctness surface around asynchronous reclamation of GPU memory. Existing heuristics (time-based trimming and LRU approximations) lead to two frequent classes of customer-visible faults: 1) stale prefix collisions where a demoted slot is overwritten while an inflight batch still references the old KV slice, and 2) non-deterministic latency spikes or OOMs when reclamation runs synchronously in the hot path.

Goal: Design and implement a tiered demotion + lease coordination protocol that ensures KV reads observed by an inference request are linearizable with respect to demotion and reclamation events, while preserving continuous batching throughput and keeping per-request latency within SLOs. The protocol should support prefix-scoped cohorts, TTL demotion, and fast-path soft-demotions that are reversible without expensive synchronizations.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime & infra leads
Unit/property tests demonstrating linearizability invariants under adversarial reorderings
Integration tests with continuous-batching harness showing <1% additional p50 token latency at steady state
Graceful fallback path that avoids correctness violations on model/variant switch
Monitoring dashboards and alerts for miss-rate, demotion-fence-wait-time, and lease-linger-count
implementation_notes: Core pieces: 1) Lease tokens per KV slot issued at read-time; token includes epoch and demotion-tier. 2) Demotion tiers: HOT->WARM->COLD where HOT is pinned for inflight batches, WARM admits soft demotion (copy-on-read) and COLD marks for reclamation. 3) Per-prefix demotion fence: a lightweight monotonic counter per prefix that readers check to ensure fence <= token. 4) Background demotion worker advances tiers using batching-aware windowing and can promote back to HOT on reuse. 5) Fast invalidation path for model rollouts that escalates fences and drains inflight tokens with bounded wait.
comments: 2026-02-19: Initial scoping meeting — agreed on tiered model and lease tokens. Action: prepare design doc and proto APIs. (Sofia)
2026-02-26: Design review — runtime leads raised concern about per-request overhead for token checks; suggested encoding token checks into existing batch metadata to amortize cost. (Daniel)
2026-03-03: Prototype complete — microbenchmark shows 3% p50 overhead with naive token checks, reduced to 0.4% after batch-metadata integration. (Daniel)
2026-03-10: Safety review — confirmed that fast invalidation requires a short global drain window; proposed default drain=50ms with config knob. (Security & Reliability)
2026-03-12: PR opened for runtime + agent changes: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4281. Requesting in-review and QA on fuzz harness. (Sofia)
tests: Property tests: assert linearizability under concurrent read/demote/reclaim operations (fuzz 1M ops)
Integration: continuous-batching harness with variable sequence lengths and prefix skews (100k requests)
Fault injection: force delayed demotion-worker and simulate node GC + OOM scenarios
Performance: steady-state throughput test with 100 concurrent batchers, track p50/p95 token latency
rollout_plan: Feature gated rollout: 1) deploy demotion-worker and token encoding behind feature flag to 10% of host pool, 2) enable lease checks in read-path for those hosts, 3) run canary for 48h with guardrails (miss-rate < +2%, p95 latency delta < +5%), 4) expand to 50% then 100% if metrics stable. If correctness regressions observed, flip feature flag to fallback synchronous invalidation for affected prefixes. Update console dashboards to surface per-prefix fence lag.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: excessive metadata increases GPU memory and per-request CPU load. Mitigation: compact token to 64bits, piggyback on existing batch metadata to avoid extra roundtrips. Risk: long-lived WARM entries delaying reclamation -> mitigation: configurable TTL per-tier and adaptive demotion aggressiveness based on observed reuse patterns. Risk: model rollout race -> mitigation: forced escalation path that stalls new batches for at most configured drain window.
